correctness.rationale: For a reset word, final trajectory positions are \(x+B+dK_x\pmod n\). Coprimality makes the effective a-jump counts occupy every residue, forcing at least \(n-1\) effective jumps on some trajectory and \(n-d\) rotations between each consecutive pair. This gives a word-length lower bound. The map \(ab^{n-d}\) fixes zero and subtracts \(d\) on nonzero states, proving the explicit matching construction. Equality fixes all a and b positions, hence uniqueness. Noncoprime jumps conserve residue differences modulo the greatest common divisor. Subset-BFS checker independently confirms all 55 parameter pairs through n=11 and constructive word through n=100.

originality.rationale: Genuinely different sharp, all-parameter reset threshold and literal uniqueness claim, beyond known synchronization criteria and uniform quadratic bounds. The two nearest open full texts and previously recorded claims were compared by hypothesis and implication; some early full texts remain uninspected and residual priority risk is acknowledged.
residual_risks: Older sources on cyclic SI-automata may contain an equivalent formula in a different labeling, especially Rystsov (2000), for which only the abstract could be checked.
The author-uploaded textual extraction of Rystsov (2022) has unreadable mathematical passages; an implicit direct specialization cannot be conclusively ruled out.
The complete MFCS 2017 paper was not inspected, though its abstract discusses a different global attained-threshold problem.
Self-review and bounded numerical checks do not substitute for an independent peer assessment.

value.rationale: The cycle plus a single unitary jump is a canonical two-letter synchronization family. The result upgrades the old uniform quadratic bound and coprime synchronizability criterion to an exact two-parameter phase diagram, with a unique optimal literal reset instruction sequence; this is structurally relevant to shortest reset synthesis and the extremal Černý example. For \(d>1\) the bound is strictly improved, and at \(d=n-1\) is linear. It is neither finite-table extraction nor a parameter substitution into a previously stated exact formula.
